root_cause.text: The SPI core’s device-registration path called spi_setup() without distinguishing initial setup from later reconfiguration, so when controller setup allocated resources and a later error occurred during initial registration, spi_cleanup() was not invoked and controller-owned resources for the spi_device leaked.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes __spi_add_device() from `spi_setup(spi)` to `__spi_setup(spi, true)` and adds an `err_cleanup:` path in `__spi_setup()` that calls `spi_cleanup(spi)` only for `initial_setup`, with the commit message explicitly stating this is needed "if spi_setup() fails while registering a device to avoid leaking any resources allocated by setup()."

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a forward declaration for `__spi_setup()` so it can be referenced earlier in the file with its full signature.
intent_record.what: A new forward declaration was added near the top of the file: `static int __spi_setup(struct spi_device *spi, bool initial_setup);`.
intent_record.how: This makes the compiler aware of the internal `__spi_setup` function signature before its definition or use later in the file, allowing earlier references to the function and ensuring type-checked calls with the added `bool initial_setup` parameter.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the internal SPI setup path with the registration-time flag when adding a device so it is configured correctly during device creation.
intent_record.what: The call to spi_setup(spi) in __spi_add_device() was replaced with a call to __spi_setup(spi, true).
intent_record.how: At runtime, device setup during SPI device addition now uses the internal setup helper with an explicit boolean argument, which changes this path to invoke setup with the specific internal mode indicated by true instead of the generic wrapper, likely ensuring the device is configured with the intended registration-time behavior.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor SPI setup by converting `spi_setup` into an internal helper with an `initial_setup` flag for differentiated in-file setup handling.
intent_record.what: The public function definition `int spi_setup(struct spi_device *spi)` was replaced with a new static function definition `static int __spi_setup(struct spi_device *spi, bool initial_setup)`, and the preceding kernel-doc comment block describing `spi_setup` was removed from this location.
intent_record.how: This changes the symbol from a globally visible setup function to an internal helper with an added boolean parameter, enabling callers in this file to distinguish initial setup from other setup paths while preventing external linkage through this definition point.

intent_record.intent_summary: Route spi_set_cs_timing() failures through the common cleanup path in spi_setup() so error handling performs proper cleanup before returning.
intent_record.what: In spi_setup(), the error path after a failed call to spi_set_cs_timing(spi) was changed from directly returning status to jumping to the err_cleanup label with goto err_cleanup.
intent_record.how: Instead of exiting immediately on spi_set_cs_timing() failure, execution now follows the shared cleanup path, ensuring any additional teardown or state restoration in err_cleanup is performed before returning the error.

intent_record.intent_summary: Route spi_setup() power-up failures through the common cleanup path so resources and state are properly cleaned up before returning an error.
intent_record.what: In spi_setup(), the error path after a failed device power-up was changed from directly returning `status` to jumping to the `err_cleanup` label with `goto err_cleanup`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, a power-up failure no longer exits the function immediately; instead, execution now follows the shared cleanup path, ensuring any required teardown or state cleanup associated with this failure path is performed before returning the error.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor SPI device setup by moving the implementation behind `__spi_setup()` with conditional initial-setup cleanup while keeping `spi_setup()` as a wrapper.
intent_record.what: The existing body of `spi_setup(struct spi_device *spi)` is split so that its main implementation now ends with an `err_cleanup:` label that conditionally calls `spi_cleanup(spi)` when `initial_setup` is true, then returns `status`; after that, a new documented wrapper function `spi_setup(struct spi_device *spi)` is added which simply returns `__spi_setup(spi, false)`.
intent_record.how: This introduces a lower-level setup path that distinguishes normal setup from an initial setup case via an `initial_setup` flag, ensuring cleanup is performed only for initial setup failures while preserving the public `spi_setup()` API as a wrapper for the non-initial case.

consistency_review.core_intent: Refactor SPI device setup by introducing an internal __spi_setup() helper with an initial-setup flag and keeping spi_setup() as a wrapper, including the needed forward declaration.
Ensure spi_setup() routes setup-time failures through a common cleanup path so resources and device state are properly unwound before returning errors.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly introduces an internal __spi_setup() with an initial-setup flag so the SPI core can distinguish first-time registration from later reconfiguration, which is the key mechanism needed to trigger proper cleanup on initial-registration errors and avoid leaking controller-allocated resources.

The change directly addresses the root cause by switching device registration to the internal SPI setup path that marks the call as happening during initial registration, enabling correct handling of setup/cleanup semantics for registration-time errors and preventing leaked controller resources.

The changes make spi_setup() send setup-time failures through the shared cleanup path, ensuring resources/state are unwound on initial setup errors. That directly addresses the root cause where initial registration failures skipped cleanup and leaked controller-owned resources.

candidates.rationale: During device registration this called the generic setup path without indicating it was an initial setup, so later registration errors could not trigger the controller-resource cleanup needed for first-time setup allocations.
This early return on spi_set_cs_timing() failure bypassed the common error-unwind path, preventing cleanup such as spi_cleanup() after setup-time resource allocation.
This early return on power-up failure similarly skipped the shared cleanup path, allowing resources allocated by controller setup during initial registration to leak.

vuln_statements.explanation: This device-registration call used the generic setup path without marking the operation as an initial setup. As a result, when later registration steps failed after controller setup had allocated resources, the code path did not treat the failure as needing first-time cleanup, leading to leaked controller-owned resources.

This early return in spi_setup() on spi_set_cs_timing() failure bypassed the common error-unwind path, so cleanup such as spi_cleanup() was not run after setup-time allocations had already been performed.
This early return in spi_setup() on power-up failure likewise skipped the shared cleanup path, preventing cleanup of resources allocated during controller setup in the initial registration flow.
